newsitem.title: INDIA: India says 95/96 money policy may have been tight.
newsitem.headline: India says 95/96 money policy may have been tight.

text.p: The Indian government said on Tuesday that a tightening of monetary policy in 1995/96 (April-March) may have been too sharp, and cautioned against easing too much now.

"There is reason to believe that the tightening of monetary policy in 1995/96, to counter the inflationary effect of the surge in capital inflows and the resulting faster monetary growth in the previous year, may have been too sharp," the government said in its annual Economic Survey.
It said monetary policy had since been brought adjusted in 1996/97 to bring it into line with targets which it said are still valid.

"We must now be careful to avoid over-compensating in the opposite direction by easing money supply too far above the target level, and thus building up inflationary pressures for the next year," it said.
"Any short-term temptation of depending solely on monetary policy to solve problems arising from other policy imperatives should be avoided," it said.
